1.text: He [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) ] frowned and turned away

2.text: Because there came to him the blind man,<sup foot_note="228175">1</sup> [interrupting].

footnotes.228175: - ʿAbdullāh, the son of Umm Maktūm.

3.text: But what would make you perceive, [O Muḥammad], that perhaps he might be purified<sup foot_note="228176">1</sup>

footnotes.228176: - As a result of what he learns from you.

4.text: Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him?

5.text: As for he who thinks himself without need,<sup foot_note="228177">1</sup>

footnotes.228177: - i.e., without need of faith or need of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) . Here it is in reference to a certain influential member of the Quraysh whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had hoped to bring to Islām.

7.text: And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified.<sup foot_note="228178">1</sup>

footnotes.228178: - The Prophet (ﷺ) was responsible only for conveying the message, not for ultimate guidance.

8.text: But as for he who came to you striving [for knowledge]

11.text: No! Indeed, they [i.e., these verses] are a reminder;

12.text: So whoever wills may remember it.<sup foot_note="228179">1</sup>

footnotes.228179: - The revelation. Or "Him," i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) .

17.text: Destroyed [i.e., cursed] is man;<sup foot_note="228180">1</sup> how disbelieving is he.

footnotes.228180: - i.e., those who deny Allāh's message.

18.text: From what thing [i.e., substance] did He create him?

19.text: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him;<sup foot_note="228181">1</sup>

footnotes.228181: - His proportions, provisions, life span, etc.

20.text: Then He eased the way for him;<sup foot_note="228182">1</sup>

footnotes.228182: - Into this world (i.e., his birth) . It may also refer to life itself, which has been made easier by Allāh's guidance.

21.text: Then He causes his death and provides a grave for him.<sup foot_note="228183">1</sup>

22.text: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.

23.text: No! He [i.e., man] has not yet accomplished what He commanded him.

24.text: Then let mankind look at his food -

25.text: How We poured down water in torrents,

26.text: Then We broke open the earth, splitting [it with sprouts],

27.text: And caused to grow within it grain

32.text: [As] enjoyment [i.e., provision] for you and your grazing livestock.

33.text: But when there comes the Deafening Blast<sup foot_note="228184">1</sup>

footnotes.228184: - The piercing blast of the Horn which signals resurrection. Aṣ-Ṣākhkhah is also a name for the Day of Resurrection.

34.text: On the Day a man will flee from his brother

35.text: And his mother and his father

36.text: And his wife and his children,

37.text: For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.<sup foot_note="228185">1</sup>

footnotes.228185: - i.e., to occupy him. He will be concerned only with himself, thus forgetting all others.

38.text: [Some] faces, that Day, will be bright -

40.text: And [other] faces, that Day, will have upon them dust.

42.text: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones.
